key_insight: Physics-Informed Neural Networks recover the global evolution of multidimensional turbulent, self-gravitating molecular clouds while showing weak training-cost dependence on spatial resolution.
engineering_relevance: PINNs offer a promising mesh-free complement to grid-based solvers for computationally demanding self-gravitating flow simulations.
method: Embed governing physics equations in the neural-network training objective.
Model isothermal clouds with astrophysically motivated turbulence in 2D and 3D.
Benchmark predicted density and velocity fields against Athena++ finite-volume simulations.
evidence_signal: Across turbulent realizations, subsonic and supersonic regimes, and dimensionalities, PINNs accurately recover global evolution over multiple free-fall times; reported training cost rises by less than 25% from 128³ to 1024³.
watch_item: Global agreement does not establish fidelity to small-scale turbulent structures, and weak training-cost scaling alone does not demonstrate an end-to-end speed advantage over Athena++.
paper_title: Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows
